title: On-call & Incident Response: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, and Comms Templates
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response standards: the end-to-end incident lifecycle, runbook conventions, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation guidance, recommended game day exercises, and production-ready status page and customer communication templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product teams responsible for operating production inference services.

Scope & Purpose

- Scope: Host API, Dedicated, and Private control plane components, core serving runtime, and the observability/alerting pipeline.
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for incidents, ensure consistent communications (internal and external), and produce actionable postmortems that prevent recurrence.

Key Roles and Responsibilities

1) Pager (Primary): First responder responsible for surface-level triage and immediate mitigation (15-minute response target).
2) Incident Commander (IC): Owns incident lifecycle, prioritization, and stakeholder updates.
3) Scribe: Records timeline, actions, and status page drafts.
4) Service Owner: Teams owning the affected service; responsible for root-cause investigation and remediation.
5) Communications Lead: Owns external messaging (status page, customer emails) and legal/security notifications if required.

Incident Severities and SLOs

- Sev 1 (P0): Major customer impact (service down, data loss, SLA breach). Response target: pager within 5 minutes; IC assigned within 10 minutes; public status page within 10 minutes.
- Sev 2 (P1): Degraded functionality with significant user impact. Response: pager within 15 minutes; IC within 30 minutes.
- Sev 3 (P2): Minor degradation or internal-only impact. Response: pager within 1 hour.

SLOs (examples):
- Control plane API availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Hosted inference tail latency (99th percentile): < 500ms for short requests.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): < 10 minutes for Sev1.

Incident Lifecycle (high level)

1) Detect/Alerting
- Alerts originate from: metrics (Prometheus), traces (Jaeger/Tempo), logs (ELK/CloudWatch), synthetic monitoring, or customer reports via Support.
- Alerts should include runbook link, severity, suggested playbook, and runbook owner.

2) Triage
- Pager checks: is alert noisy / redundant? Run initial health checks (see Runbook Checklist).
- If confirmed, escalate to IC and open an incident channel (Slack #incident-<id>), create incident page (Confluence), and update status page to "investigating" for Sev1/Sev2.

3) Mitigation & Recovery
- Execute mitigation steps from the relevant runbook. Aim to restore customer-facing functionality first (fallback model, route to Dedicated capacity, enable degraded mode).
- IC coordinates cross-team actions and approves external communications.

4) Post-Incident
- Transition to postmortem once service is stable and metrics are normal for a monitoring window (typically 24-72 hours depending on severity).
- Postmortem due: Sev1 within 5 business days draft; final within 15 business days. Sev2 within 10 business days.

Runbook Conventions

- Each runbook must include: scope, owner, contact list, detection signals, required dashboards, quick check commands, mitigation steps (ordered by impact), rollback steps, post-incident notes, and related pages.
- File naming: <service>-runbook-<component>. Examples: runtime-kv-cache-runbook, api-gateway-dns-runbook.
- Keep runbooks short, prioritized checklists that can be executed under stress.

Runbook Checklist (example quick checks)

- Verify alert: check metric graphs (Prometheus) for spikes or drops.
- Health checks: curl -fsS https://controlplane.redwood.internal/healthz || echo "unhealthy"
- Check pods: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime -o wide
- Check logs (last 15m): kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/runtime --since=15m | tail -n 200
- Check long-running RPCs and queue depth: grafana dashboard links included in runbook.

Example Runbook: runtime-kv-cache

Title: runtime-kv-cache-runbook
Owner: eng-serving-runtime
Detection: High token generation latency correlated with KV cache misses; increased GPU utilization and retry rates.
Quick checks:
- gremlin query: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $READ_ONLY_TOKEN" "https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_miss_rate%5B5m%5D"
- Check cache hit ratio graph and recent commits to kernel selector.
Mitigation steps (ordered):
1) Trigger soft restart of runtime workers in affected AZ: kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime --namespace=redwood --field-selector metadata.name=runtime-worker-<az>
2) If soft restart fails, scale up worker replicas by +20%: kubectl scale deploy/runtime --replicas=<current+1> -n redwood
3) Fallback routing: switch traffic to last-known-good model variant by adjusting routing policy in Traffic Router console (documented link).
4) If GPU memory corruption suspected, evict affected nodes and reassign workloads to spare pool.
Post-incident: add histogram of cache misses to runbook, add alerts for unusual miss-rate gradients.

Postmortem Template (required fields)

- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Affected Services/Customers
- Start / End / Detection / Mitigation timestamps (UTC)
- Summary (one-paragraph impact statement)
- Timeline (ordered events with timestamps)
- Root cause analysis (RCA) — clear, evidence-backed explanation
- Corrective actions (short-term mitigations)
- Preventative actions (longer-term fixes) with owners and target dates
- Rollback / rollback safe states (if applicable)
- Customer impact and communications (links to status page and emails sent)
- Lessons learned and follow-ups

Example Postmortem snippet:

Summary: On 2026-01-12 at 14:07 UTC a regression in kernel selection logic increased KV cache miss rate and caused a 35% increase in 99p latency for hosted text generation for ~42 minutes. Customers on the shared tier experienced request failures and elevated latency.
Root cause: A change to the kernel selector introduced an edge case that bypassed a warm-up path for newly loaded model shards, causing sustained cache misses under burst traffic.
Action items:
- Revert kernel-selector change (owner: runtime-team, due: 2026-01-13)
- Add pre-deploy automated regression test around cache warm-up (owner: qa, due: 2026-02-01)
- Add alert for sustained miss-rate delta > 5% over 10 minutes (owner: eng-sre, due: 2026-01-20)

On-call Rotations and Escalation Policy

- Rotation model: primary + secondary per week (7-day rotations). Each primary is supported by a secondary who must be available for immediate escalation. For high-risk services, use 24/7 pager splits with 12-hour shifts.
- Handoff checklist (before shift change):
  1) Confirm no active incidents for your services in the last 30 minutes.
  2) Review outstanding action items and update incident page.
  3) Verify contact list and ensure pager is functional.
  4) Confirm personal escalation path and ensure Slack DND is disabled for critical alerts.
- Escalation policy: on missed ack (MTTA target exceeded) escalate to secondary, then on-call manager, then engineering lead. Escalation contact list maintained in the oncall roster.

Game Days (exercise program)

Purpose: Validate runbooks, test fallback paths, rehearse cross-team coordination, and identify monitoring gaps.

Recommended cadence and example exercises:
- Quarterly service-level game days for top 10 customer-facing services.
- Example: Simulate a model-serving node loss in a single AZ and exercise routing to Dedicated capacity, verify status page updates, and validate customer-facing degraded-mode behavior.
- Post-game-day: produce a short readout with findings and 2-3 action items.

Status Page & Customer Communications Templates

Status page states: investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved. For all Sev1/Sev2 incidents update public status as early as possible and then follow the cadence: initial (investigating), update (identified/mitigating), update (monitoring), update (resolved).

Status Page Template (short):
- Title: Partial outage affecting Hosted API text generation
- Time started: 2026-02-10T15:42:00Z
- Impact: Some customers experienced increased latency and failed requests for text generation.
- Current status: Investigating (or Identified/Mitigating/Monitoring/Resolved)
- Next update: 15 minutes
- Mitigation: Traffic is being diverted to Dedicated capacity for impacted customers; engineers are investigating a regression in the runtime kernel selector.

Customer Email Template (Sev1 initial)

Subject: Incident: Partial outage impacting Redwood Hosted API (ongoing)

Hello,

We are currently investigating an issue affecting the Redwood Hosted API text generation endpoints that may cause increased latency or failed requests. Our engineering team is actively investigating and we will provide an update within 15 minutes. We apologize for the disruption.

What we know:
- Start time: 2026-02-10 15:42 UTC
- Impact: increased latency and request failures for a subset of text-generation requests

What we’re doing:
- Routing traffic to Dedicated pools for affected customers, live rollback of recent runtime selector changes, and monitoring of telemetry.

If you have critical questions or require an SLA credit assessment, please contact support@redwood.ai with your account ID.

Thank you for your patience — Redwood Support

Internal Incident Channel Template (Slack pinned message)

- Incident ID: INC-20260210-001
- Severity: Sev1
- IC: @maya.chen
- Scribe: @diego.martinez
- Short summary: Elevated 99p latency and request failures; traffic being routed to Dedicated pool; investigating kernel selector regression.
- Links: runbook, dashboards, logs, status-page

Post-Incident Communication (final customer message)

Subject: Resolved: Partial outage impacting Redwood Hosted API on 2026-02-10

Hello,

The issue affecting text-generation endpoints has been resolved as of 2026-02-10 16:24 UTC. Root cause: regression in runtime kernel selector that increased KV cache misses under burst traffic. We reverted the change and validated system stability. A follow-up postmortem will be published with corrective actions and timelines.

We apologize for the impact and appreciate your patience.

Action items for engineers (template checklists)

- Post-incident immediate: add timeline to incident page, label relevant commits, assign RCA owner, and schedule postmortem meeting.
- Medium-term: owner to define remediation and expected release date.
- Long-term: add automated tests and monitoring to prevent regression recurrence.

Appendix A: Example Runbook Table (text table)

| Component | Owner | Quick-check | Mitigation Steps |
| runtime-kv-cache | eng-serving-runtime | cache_hit_ratio dashboard; logs | restart workers, scale replicas, route traffic |
| api-gateway | eng-platform | 5xx-rate metric; nginx logs | failover to standby gateway, rollback config |

Appendix B: Incident page checklist (create on Confluence)

- Title and Incident ID
- Severity, start time, impacted customers
- Roles (IC, Scribe, Communications)
- Timeline (live updates)
- Mitigation steps executed and who performed them
- Links to runbooks, dashboards, and PRs
- Postmortem link container

Appendix C: Contact matrix

- Pager schedule: published in People Ops oncall roster (link)
- Escalation: secondary -> on-call manager -> eng lead -> CTO (if P0 persists > 4 hours)
